definition: Onerous means burdensome; describing a duty, task, or obligation that weighs on someone as a heavy, oppressive load.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word onerous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know onerous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The lease came with onerous conditions, including weekly inspections and a security deposit worth three months' rent.
A demanding job asks a lot of you; an onerous one weighs on you like a heavy burden you can barely carry.
A crushing workload goes beyond onerous, so overwhelming that it flattens any hope of keeping up.

Burdensome means loading someone down with heavy work or worry, and it is the closest everyday twin of onerous, usually interchangeable with it. Onerous is the more formal word and clings to duties and obligations: contracts, conditions, and requirements are onerous when their weight feels oppressive.

Taxing means draining: a taxing day makes heavy demands on your energy, patience, or strength while it lasts, and the word measures the toll on you in the moment. Onerous measures the standing weight of an obligation that oppresses you between the hard days too.

Laborious means requiring long, hard work; the sweat is the point, hours of effort in the doing. Onerous is about weight rather than work: a duty can be onerous even when each task is easy, because it is imposed, endless, and oppressive to carry.
